issues.sentence: a recent benchmarking effort on unsupervised integrative clustering in TCGA colorectal cancer, for example, found SNF gave the best subtype classification accuracy, with the authors themselves emphasising that performance was highly dataset-dependent [R17]
issues.issue: The card confirms SNF had the best subtype classification accuracy, but the excerpt/key finding do not include the authors emphasising that 'performance was highly dataset-dependent'; this specific attribution to the authors is not supported by the card.
issues.fix: Remove or qualify the parenthetical, e.g. 'found SNF gave the best subtype classification accuracy [R17]'.

issues.sentence: Third, methodological novelty continues to outpace reproducible software engineering: containerised releases, version pinning and FAIR packaging remain the exception rather than the rule for these general-purpose frameworks [R27]
issues.issue: R27 describes a single multi-omics workflow (a childhood externalizing behaviour case study) that DOES implement FAIR packaging, Nextflow containers, version control and licensing. The card is itself a positive example of FAIR packaging, not evidence that such practices are 'the exception rather than the rule' across general-purpose frameworks.
issues.fix: Replace with a claim actually supported by R27, e.g. 'A model FAIR-packaged multi-omics workflow using Nextflow, containers and rich metadata is described in [R27], illustrating what the general-purpose frameworks discussed here typically lack.' Alternatively, cite a study that surveys software quality across these tools.

section: Introduction: why multi-omics integration needs dedicated software

issues.sentence: This concern is sharpened in microbiome and host-microbiome settings, where metagenomic, metatranscriptomic, metabolomic and host-response layers each have their own conventions, ontologies and batch-effect structures that must be reconciled before any joint modelling is meaningful [R1, R6, R8, R39].
issues.issue: R6 (phyloseq) and R8 (QIIME 2) are single-omics microbiome census/analysis tools that do not address reconciliation across multiple omics layers; phyloseq discusses integrating different analytical disciplines within one omics, and QIIME 2 is a general microbiome platform. The specific multi-omics reconciliation claim (across metagenomic, metatranscriptomic, metabolomic and host-response layers) is directly supported only by R1 (EasyMultiProfiler) and R39 (PALM).
issues.fix: Drop R6 and R8 from this sentence, since they do not concern multi-omics reconciliation; the claim is adequately supported by R1 and R39 alone.

issues.sentence: Even when a conceptual scheme exists, its assumptions about independence between modalities, sparsity of the signal and tolerance for missing data are not always made visible to the user [R19, R31, R35], which complicates both interpretation and reuse.
issues.issue: The cited papers are methods that explicitly model sparsity and missing-data tolerance (MLMF uses a class indicator matrix for missing omics, NetMIM uses spike-and-slab priors and FBM-style augmentation for block missingness, SigMAE is a variational Bayesian factor model). They are examples where such assumptions are made explicit in the model, not evidence that assumptions are typically hidden from users, so the cards do not support the claim of opacity.
issues.fix: Rephrase as an authorial critique (e.g., 'In our view...') without these specific citations, or replace with sources that explicitly document the problem of hidden assumptions in integration tools.

issues.sentence: MixMC extends the mixOmics framework to handle compositional 16S rRNA marker-gene data, and the broader family of regularised multi-block methods — RGCCA, O2PLS, JIVE and MCIA — likewise consolidate block-specific latent components but differ in their treatment of shared versus block-specific variance [R64, R65].
issues.issue: Two issues: (1) R64 describes MixMC as a 'novel multivariate data analysis framework' and does not explicitly state that it extends the mixOmics framework — the compositional 16S handling is supported, but the 'extends mixOmics' framing is not. (2) The claims about O2PLS, JIVE, and MCIA consolidating block-specific latent components and differing in their treatment of shared versus block-specific variance are not supported by either cited card: R64 concerns MixMC only, and R65 describes only RGCCA/SGCCA.
issues.fix: Reframe as 'MixMC provides a framework that accounts for the compositional nature of 16S rRNA data' (supported by R64), restrict the multi-block methods to RGCCA/SGCCA (supported by R65), or add cards that describe O2PLS, JIVE, and MCIA.

issues.sentence: Microbiome-specific standards — MaAsLin2 and ANCOM-BC for differential abundance testing, Anvi'o for visualisation of microbial multi-omics, and mixMC for compositional multi-block analysis — sit at a different level of the stack, providing components for integration rather than full integration strategies [R62, R63, R64].
issues.issue: Anvi'o is mentioned as a tool for visualisation of microbial multi-omics, but none of the three cited cards describes Anvi'o. R62 supports MaAsLin2, R63 supports ANCOM-BC, and R64 supports MixMC.
issues.fix: Add a card that supports Anvi'o (e.g., an Anvi'o publication), or remove Anvi'o from the enumeration.

issues.sentence: Pathway-level web platforms such as PaintOmics and 3Omics are subsumed under the knowledge-driven axis defined above [R66].
issues.issue: R66 describes 3Omics only. PaintOmics is mentioned alongside 3Omics but is not supported by R66 (or any other cited card).
issues.fix: Add a card that supports PaintOmics, or remove PaintOmics and cite only 3Omics.

section: Web servers and point-and-click platforms for multi-omics

issues.sentence: The single-cell analyst [R20] supports six single-cell omics modalities together with spatial transcriptomics, providing over twenty interactive tools that run in the browser; because the underlying card does not enumerate the six modalities, the specific assays should be verified against the platform's own documentation rather than inferred from secondary descriptions.
issues.issue: The text claims the underlying card does not enumerate the six modalities, but the R20 abstract explicitly lists them: scRNA-seq, scATAC-seq, scImmune profiling, single-cell copy number variation, cytometry by time-of-flight, and flow cytometry, plus spatial transcriptomics.
issues.fix: Cite R20 directly for the six modalities, e.g. 'The single-cell analyst [R20] supports six single-cell omics modalities (scRNA-seq, scATAC-seq, scImmune profiling, scCNV, CyTOF, flow cytometry) together with spatial transcriptomics, providing over 20 interactive tools that run in the browser.'

issues.sentence: its principal limitation, made plain by the originating study, is that it does not in itself replace either the breadth of QIIME 2's upstream processing or the depth of single-object analyses that phyloseq has accumulated over more than a decade of community use [R1].
issues.issue: The R1 abstract presents EasyMultiProfiler positively as 'directly resolving data integration issues, workflow standardization, and result reproducibility' and does not state that its principal limitation is the failure to replace QIIME 2 upstream processing or the depth of phyloseq's single-object analyses. The limitation attributed to the originating study is not supported by the available card.
issues.fix: Remove the attribution to R1 (e.g., phrase as the author's own interpretation) or remove the limitation claim. If retained as author commentary, drop '[R1]' or qualify as author's synthesis.

issues.sentence: while CPMOAD [R22], NOODAI [R51] and MONGKIE [R46] rely on a hosted service model that cannot be replicated offline.
issues.issue: R46 describes MONGKIE as developed 'in Java based on the NetBeans plugin Rich Client Platform', which indicates a downloadable/local-installable desktop application rather than a hosted-only service. The claim that MONGKIE cannot be replicated offline is contradicted by the card.
issues.fix: Remove MONGKIE from this list, e.g. 'while CPMOAD [R22] and NOODAI [R51] rely on a hosted service model that cannot be replicated offline.'

section: Data structures, workflow systems and reproducibility infrastructure

issues.sentence: MultiAssayExperiment is not without caveats — its subsetting and colData consistency can be brittle when assays arrive from heterogeneous pipelines, and the class does not, by itself, enforce semantic alignment between modalities, leaving that responsibility with the analyst [R45].
issues.issue: The R45 abstract does not mention any of these specific technical caveats (brittleness of subsetting/colData consistency, lack of semantic-alignment enforcement). R45 in fact presents MAE as reducing 'major obstacles to efficient, scalable, and reproducible statistical analysis of multiomics data,' with no caveats about heterogeneous pipelines or semantic alignment.
issues.fix: Rephrase as the author's own observation (e.g., 'In our experience…') without citing R45 for the caveats, or cite a source that actually documents these limitations.

issues.sentence: MultiAssayExperiment does not natively encode time, so dedicated frameworks such as timeOmics [R36] and netOmics [R37] wrap the Bioconductor container with explicit temporal alignment, smoothing and clustering steps
issues.issue: R36 mentions 'pre-processing, modeling and clustering' but not 'temporal alignment' or 'smoothing' as named steps. R37 does not mention any of these three steps — its abstract describes building hybrid multi-omics networks via 'smart node labelling and propagation analysis,' with no mention of temporal alignment, smoothing, or clustering.
issues.fix: Correct to something like: 'timeOmics [R36] provides pre-processing, modeling and clustering steps for longitudinal multi-omics data, while netOmics [R37] builds and explores hybrid multi-omics networks from longitudinal data using node labelling and propagation analysis.'

issues.sentence: The decision matters because it inherits, at no implementation cost, a decade of subsetting, batch-correction and differential-testing conventions already validated in oncology pipelines and in metabolomics workflows built around mixOmics [R3].
issues.issue: The R3 abstract describes mixOmics as a general R package for feature selection and integration across transcriptomics, proteomics and metabolomics; it does not mention validation in oncology pipelines. Citing R3 does not support the oncology-validation claim.
issues.fix: Restrict the R3 citation to the metabolomics claim, e.g., 'validated in metabolomics workflows built around mixOmics [R3],' and either remove the oncology claim or support it with a separate citation (oncology validation of MAE-style conventions is more naturally attributable to R45/TCGA).

issues.sentence: A comprehensive evaluation of 14 protein-abundance and chromatin-accessibility prediction algorithms and 18 single-cell integration algorithms across 47 datasets singled out totalVI and scArches for protein prediction, LS_Lab for chromatin-accessibility prediction, and Seurat, MOJITOO and UINMF as the most consistent integration performers [R26].
issues.issue: The abstract distinguishes between vertical integration (Seurat, MOJITOO, scAI) and horizontal/mosaic integration (totalVI, UINMF). The text omits scAI (a leading vertical-integration method) and groups Seurat (vertical), MOJITOO (vertical) and UINMF (horizontal/mosaic) together as 'the most consistent integration performers' without preserving this distinction.
issues.fix: Re-state as: '…Seurat, MOJITOO and scAI as leading methods for vertical integration, and totalVI and UINMF as top performers in horizontal and mosaic integration scenarios [R26].'

issues.sentence: Reviews of deep-learning approaches in tumour genomics reinforce this caveat, noting that convolutional, recurrent, graph and attention-based architectures are typically evaluated on the same handful of TCGA and METABRIC splits, with hyperparameters tuned by the developers themselves and rarely audited independently [R56].
issues.issue: The abstract does not make these specific factual claims: it does not state that DL architectures are evaluated on TCGA/METABRIC splits, that hyperparameters are tuned by developers themselves, or that evaluations are rarely audited independently. These attributions are not supported by the cited card.
issues.fix: Either cite the review's actual reported findings (model interpretability, data scarcity, computational requirements, integration challenges) or remove the specific unsupported claims about TCGA/METABRIC splits, developer-tuned hyperparameters and lack of independent auditing.

issues.sentence: Reported gains such as the 7–24 percent F-score improvement of a deep matrix-factorisation model [R12] and the BRCA/KIPAN/ROSMAP/LGG accuracies of graph-based frameworks such as MOGOLA [R52] were both measured exclusively on TCGA-derived cohorts, and their generality beyond that setting is not established.
issues.issue: ROSMAP is not a TCGA-derived cohort; it originates from the Religious Orders Study and Memory and Aging Project. The claim that all four datasets (BRCA, KIPAN, ROSMAP, LGG) were 'measured exclusively on TCGA-derived cohorts' is therefore incorrect for ROSMAP.
issues.fix: Replace 'on TCGA-derived cohorts' with 'on TCGA-derived cancer cohorts and the ROSMAP neurodegenerative cohort' or similar wording that correctly reflects that ROSMAP is non-TCGA.

issues.sentence: First, reproducibility infrastructure — version pinning, containerisation, container-tested execution, and explicit reporting of random seeds and software versions — is rarely audited, even though it is the prerequisite on which any cross-study comparison depends [R27].
issues.issue: R27 is presented as evidence that reproducibility infrastructure is 'rarely audited,' but the cited card actually describes the construction of a multi-omics workflow that explicitly implements FAIR principles, version control, containerisation, documentation and licensing — i.e., it is a positive example of good practice, not evidence that such infrastructure is rarely audited. The citation does not support the claim it is attached to.
issues.fix: Either cite a card that explicitly documents the lack of reproducibility auditing across the field, or remove the citation after 'is rarely audited' and reposition R27 to support the separate claim that reproducibility infrastructure is a prerequisite (e.g., '…cross-study comparison depends, as exemplified by FAIR Digital Object workflows [R27]').

section: EasyMultiProfiler (EMP): design, strengths and limitations relative to the alternatives

issues.sentence: The same cannot be said of pipelines implemented purely in ad hoc Python or Snakemake scripts without typed container classes, where reproducibility depends entirely on workflow-manager pinning and external checksum capture [R27].
issues.issue: R27 describes a Nextflow pipeline that explicitly uses containers and implements FAIR practices, not 'ad hoc Python or Snakemake scripts without typed container classes'. The card states: 'The analysis workflow was implemented as a modular pipeline in the workflow manager Nextflow, including containers with software dependencies.' R27 is therefore neither about Python/Snakemake nor about pipelines lacking container-based reproducibility.
issues.fix: R27 does not support the claim about Python or Snakemake scripts lacking typed container classes. Either drop the citation, or revise the sentence so the cited card actually backs it (e.g., cite R27 for a Nextflow+containers+FAIR example rather than for an 'ad hoc script' counter-example).

issues.sentence: By anchoring itself to them, EMP inherits the same provenance tracking, batch-aware accessors and ready-to-analyse objects that already power TCGA-scale cancer multi-omics work [R45].
issues.issue: R45's abstract supports only 'ready-to-analyse objects' and the TCGA-scale cancer multi-omics context. The specific features 'provenance tracking' and 'batch-aware accessors' are not mentioned in the R45 abstract excerpt.
issues.fix: Restrict the claim to what R45 explicitly supports, e.g., 'the same ready-to-analyse objects that already power TCGA-scale cancer multi-omics work', or remove the unsupported specific features.

issues.sentence: reviews of spatial multi-omics catalogue technical noise, batch effects and calibration drift as unresolved challenges [R59]
issues.issue: The card [R59] mentions 'technical noise' and 'batch effects' but does not mention 'calibration drift' as an unresolved challenge.
issues.fix: Remove 'and calibration drift' or cite a card that does discuss calibration drift.

issues.sentence: surveys of AI in viral and stem-cell multi-omics repeatedly invoke the same shortcomings without offering remediating tooling [R57, R58]
issues.issue: Card [R57] explicitly states it has 'highlighted future directions that would help in enhancing AI assisted multi-omics research,' which contradicts the claim that it offers no remediating tooling. Card [R58] similarly discusses cautious use of AI as a decision-support tool rather than framing limitations as wholly unaddressed.
issues.fix: Soften the claim (e.g., 'offer only limited remediating tooling' rather than 'without offering remediating tooling').

issues.sentence: Newer frameworks such as Kolmogorov–Arnold network-based models [R14], graph neural network pipelines [R11], graph-embedded deep generative clustering [R13] and semi-supervised deep matrix factorisation [R12] report quantitative gains on TCGA cohorts but offer little insight into the biological provenance of their latent dimensions.
issues.issue: Only [R12] (SSD-MO) explicitly reports evaluation on TCGA datasets. [R14] (MOKAN) does not specify TCGA, [R11] (BioNeuralNet) is described as a general framework with no TCGA mention, and [R13] (GeDGC) operates on single-cell data on 'ten datasets' with no TCGA mention.
issues.fix: Restrict the TCGA-gain claim to [R12] (and possibly others explicitly tested on TCGA), or qualify the sentence (e.g., 'on the cohorts they were tested on').

issues.sentence: Even when attention or gating mechanisms are introduced ostensibly for interpretability [R47, R52], validation is typically limited to ablation studies rather than to perturbation or experimental confirmation.
issues.issue: Card [R52] (MOGOLA) explicitly mentions ablation studies, but card [R47] (MO-GCAN) does not mention ablation studies in the abstract — it describes evaluation via test accuracy, training time, precision, recall and F-score.
issues.fix: Drop [R47] from the citation supporting the ablation-studies claim, or qualify the sentence as 'sometimes' rather than 'typically.'

issues.sentence: Sharma and colleagues did not evaluate alignment with clinically deployed intrinsic subtypes when they applied MOFA+ to a 335-patient breast cancer cohort and identified three multi-omics clusters with distinct long-term prognoses validated in METABRIC and TCGA [R25]
issues.issue: The card [R25] explicitly states that 'a lack of prognostic association to long-term follow-up above 12 years in the previously established intrinsic subtypes was shown for these cohorts,' meaning Sharma and colleagues DID evaluate alignment with intrinsic subtypes (and found a lack of long-term prognostic association), contrary to the claim that they 'did not evaluate alignment with clinically deployed intrinsic subtypes.'
issues.fix: Correct to: 'did not find significant prognostic alignment of their multi-omics clusters with clinically deployed intrinsic subtypes at long-term follow-up, having explicitly shown a lack of long-term prognostic association in intrinsic subtypes'.

issues.sentence: single-cell platforms such as the single-cell analyst [R20], Profiler [R16] and Seurat-based pipelines serve yet another community
issues.issue: Card [R16] (Profiler) does not describe Profiler as a single-cell platform. The abstract states it supports 'proteomics, transcriptomics, lipidomics, and electroencephalogram data' (e.g., glioblastoma, pancancer), with no mention of single-cell omics.
issues.fix: Remove [R16] from this single-cell grouping, or replace with a tool that is genuinely a single-cell platform.

issues.sentence: QIIME 2 generalised this logic into a plugin-based, artefact-centric platform with semantically typed data objects and provenance tracking [R8]
issues.issue: The R8 card does not explicitly confirm that QIIME 2 is 'artefact-centric' or uses 'semantically typed data objects'. The card only states QIIME 2 is 'reproducible, interactive, scalable and extensible' and supports 'standardized, shareable processing'. While 'extensible' implies plugin-based architecture and 'standardized, shareable' is consistent with provenance tracking, the specific architectural descriptors 'artefact-centric' and 'semantically typed' are not supported by the (very sparse) card.
issues.fix: Remove the unsupported architectural descriptors, e.g., 'QIIME 2 generalised this logic into a plugin-based, extensible platform supporting standardised, shareable processing and analysis of microbiome data within reproducible workflows [R8]', or cite a source that explicitly documents QIIME 2's artefact/semantic-type system.

section: Recommendations for users and developers, roadmap and conclusions

issues.sentence: For pathway-level interpretation, multi-view PLS approaches such as DIABLO and the more recent PathIntegrate convert molecular features to pathway scores before modelling, which is closer to the mechanistic language clinicians expect [R30, R44].
issues.issue: R44 (DIABLO) does not support the claim that DIABLO converts molecular features to pathway scores before modelling. DIABLO operates directly on molecular features (mRNA, miRNA, CpG, protein, metabolite) using PLS-based latent components to identify discriminative variables; it does not perform pathway-score conversion. Only R30 (PathIntegrate) explicitly converts molecular features to pathway-level scores via single-sample pathway analysis.
issues.fix: Rephrase so that only PathIntegrate is credited with the molecular-to-pathway conversion, e.g., 'multi-view PLS approaches such as DIABLO operate on molecular features, while PathIntegrate converts molecular features to pathway scores before modelling, which is closer to the mechanistic language clinicians expect.'

issues.sentence: The reported 7–24% F-score gain of SSD-MO over baselines on six TCGA cancer datasets is informative but is not known to generalise to non-cancer, longitudinal or microbiome data
issues.issue: The abstract reports two distinct ranges: 9–24% over unsupervised baselines and 7–20% over semi-supervised benchmarks. Collapsing these into a single '7–24% over baselines' range loses the distinction between comparison types and slightly misrepresents the lower bound for the unsupervised comparison.
issues.fix: Cite the two ranges separately, e.g., 'The reported 9–24% F-score gain of SSD-MO over unsupervised baselines and 7–20% over semi-supervised benchmarks on six TCGA cancer datasets is informative but is not known to generalise to non-cancer, longitudinal or microbiome data'.
